problem:
Consider the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t).$ Which of the following vectors are solutions to this equation?

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}t \\ 5t\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2} \\ 2t-8\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Solutions to a Matrix Differential Equation
examples.problem:
Consider the matrix differential equation $[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}]$ Which of the following vectors are solutions to this equation?

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{5t} \\ 5{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Here, we need to substitute each vector into the given matrix differential equation and check if it results in a true statement.

For $\mathbf{x}_1(t),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{(3{e}^{5t})}^{′} \\ {(5{e}^{-3t})}^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{e}^{5t} \\ 5{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}15{e}^{5t} \\ -15{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{e}^{5t} \\ 5{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}15{e}^{5t} \\ -15{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}15{e}^{5t} \\ -15{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for $\mathbf{x}_2(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{(t+5)}^{′} \\ {({t}^{2}-3)}^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}t+5 \\ {t}^{2}-3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2t\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}t+5 \\ {t}^{2}-3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2t\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}5t+25 \\ -3{t}^{2}+9\end{aligned}].\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for $\mathbf{x}_3(t),$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{(5{e}^{t})}^{′} \\ {(-3{e}^{t})}^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5{e}^{t} \\ -3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{t} \\ -3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5{e}^{t} \\ -3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{t} \\ -3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}25{e}^{t} \\ 9{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$\mathbf{x}_1(t)$ only."

feedback.problem:
Which of the following systems are homogeneous?

- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(6t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)+2{t}^{3}\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)+4{e}^{t} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t)-4{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5){x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a first-order linear system of differential equations with two dependent variables is a system of the form

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=a(t){x}_{1}(t)+b(t){x}_{2}(t)+f(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=c(t){x}_{1}(t)+d(t){x}_{2}(t)+g(t).\end{aligned}
$$

If $f≡0$ and $g≡0$ (i.e., both $f$ and $g$ are zero functions), then the system is *homogeneous*. Otherwise, if at least one of $f$ or $g$ is not identically zero, the system is *inhomogeneous*.

With this in mind, let's inspect each system:

- System I is inhomogeneous since it can be written in the standard form with $f≢0$ and $g≢0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t)=-3, &  & b(t)=1, &  & f(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(6t) \\ c(t)=1, &  & d(t)=-2, &  & g(t)=2{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

- System II is inhomogeneous since it can be written in the standard form with $f≢0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t)=1, &  & b(t)=3, &  & f(t)=4{e}^{t} \\ c(t)=1, &  & d(t)=-1, &  & g(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$

- System III is homogeneous since it can be written in the standard form with $f≡0$ and $g≡0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t)=-4, &  & b(t)=1, &  & f(t)=0 \\ c(t)=1, &  & d(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5), &  & g(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
